summary: Serverless Supabase on Vercel with PostgreSQL as the database in India; front end: Next.js, React Native.

frontend.justification: Web: One React codebase gives SSR/SSG pages for SEO and app-style screens. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript/TypeScript; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to marketplace projects; seo_critical=true and it serves pre-rendered HTML. Mobile: Shares JavaScript/TypeScript skills and code with the web team. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript/TypeScript; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to marketplace projects.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.1 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to marketplace projects).
Scored 0.1 points lower: limited camera/GPS access.

tradeoffs: App Router and server/client component split add conceptual weight.
Best features assume a Node/serverless host; static export loses SSR.
JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
backend.justification: One managed Postgres project gives auth, storage, realtime and APIs. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript/TypeScript; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to marketplace projects; native WebSocket/real-time support.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.6 points lower: the chosen option wins on requirements.realtime (native WebSocket/real-time support).
Scored 3.7 points lower: the chosen option wins on timeline.mvp_weeks (a 3-person team ships in 8 weeks without building auth/storage).
Excluded: Firebase (Google) stores Firebase Authentication data in the US (Firestore itself can run in Mumbai) (infrastructure.data_residency).

tradeoffs: Business logic split across RLS policies, SQL and Edge Functions is harder to test.
Free projects pause after a week of inactivity; production needs the Pro plan.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: ACID transactions keep bookings and payouts consistent; well suited to marketplace projects; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; strong cost, which you rated 4/5. Data stays in South Asia (Mumbai, ap-south-1) to satisfy data_residency=india. Existing data is handled as described in the migration plan (supporting services).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.6 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to marketplace projects).
Scored 10.3 points lower: time-series extension adds operations without a time-series need; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to marketplace projects).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Zero-config Next.js hosting with preview deploys and Mumbai (bom1) functions. Fit for this project: strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; Vercel builds and serves Next.js natively.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.1 points lower: static hosting only; the API must run elsewhere.
Scored 0.5 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.

tradeoffs: Hobby (free) plan is non-commercial only; commercial use needs Pro ($20/member).

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; issues JWTs that Postgres RLS policies check. Phone OTP is sent through MSG91; in India every SMS template and sender ID must be registered on the TRAI DLT platform first.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor; user data stored in the US.
Firebase Authentication processes data in the US.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: UPI, cards and netbanking; Route splits each payment between the platform commission and the provider's linked account, which is what a services marketplace needs.

alternatives.why_not: Similar split-payments product; fewer SDK examples.
Invite-only for new Indian businesses.

tradeoffs: Gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are not part of the infra estimate.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Another vendor; Supabase Storage enforces the same RLS rules.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; pushes chat messages and booking/job-status changes to subscribed clients over WebSockets.

alternatives.why_not: An extra service to run.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections need sticky sessions or a pub/sub layer.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, image/file processing, notifications) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.choice: PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector + GIN, pg_trgm for typos)
supporting.justification: At 30000 users and ~50 GB the database's own search is fast enough, transactional and needs no sync pipeline.

alternatives.why_not: Better typo tolerance and ranking, but another service to keep in sync; move to it if search becomes core.
Over-sized at this scale.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android for booking and job-status updates.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.choice: Migration and integration plan for existing systems
supporting.justification: CentOS 7 servers: do not deploy new services there; move workloads to the recommended hosting and decommission once empty. Node.js 16 API: keep it running behind the new API (strangler pattern) and move endpoints one at a time; upgrade the runtime first if it is end-of-life. MySQL 5.7 database: migrate to PostgreSQL with pgloader; run both in parallel with change-data-capture until cut-over, then retire the old server. AngularJS admin panel: replace screen by screen in the recommended front end; link both from one navigation until the old UI is empty.

alternatives.why_not: Higher risk: everything switches at once with no fallback.

tradeoffs: Running old and new systems in parallel costs extra for a few weeks.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosted server to maintain.

supporting.justification: Free tier for logs/metrics; scrub personal data before export since data residency applies.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L2: ~30000 users, ~800 peak concurrent, ~160 req/s at peak, ~50 GB stored
Supabase Pro ($25/month) for production: free projects pause when idle and include ~1 GB of file storage
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: Existing system 'CentOS 7 servers': CentOS Linux is end-of-life; move to RHEL, AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux. Source: https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/linux/centos-linux-eol
Existing system 'Node.js 16 API': End-of-life Node.js release (Node 20 ended 30 Apr 2026). Source: https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases
Existing system 'MySQL 5.7 database': MySQL 5.7 ended Oct 2023 and 8.0 ended Apr 2026; move to 8.4 LTS. Source: https://endoflife.date/mysql
Existing system 'AngularJS admin panel': AngularJS support ended 31 Dec 2021. Source: https://docs.angularjs.org/misc/version-support-status
Upper estimate ($213) exceeds the $150 budget; watch usage as you grow.
Taking payments: use the gateway's hosted checkout/SDK so card data never touches your servers (PCI DSS SAQ A).
DPDP Act 2023: collect consent per purpose, honour erasure requests and report breaches; the Act itself does not force India-only storage unless data_residency requires it.
